Closing the space between the plots
Direction B — one answer, then the evidence

Option B — rail inside today's 1,240 band
Option C — location in the frozen header

annotations.text:
WHAT IS IN THE WORKBOOK
A 1,482 px band on six even pairs of 247. Frozen: the header, the project line, six tiles in one row, the verdict. Then the two key plots with the project location beside them, then two rows of three, then a key row, then every table. Header through the supporting plots is 613 px, inside the 624 a 15.6 in screen at 125% scaling gives Excel.

THE PLOTS
They touch, on one hairline. Six chart legends became the single key row under the section charts — charts 3, 4 and 5 all used chart 2's four alternative colours, and 6 and 7 the same four layer colours. No chart names an axis its own title already names.

NOT TAKEN, KEPT FOR THE ARGUMENT
Direction B put the answer in one panel beside the plots instead of six tiles and a banner, which returns 133 px at the top but stops the answer being frozen while you scroll. Direction C lifted the results table above the fold, at the price of every chart but the key pair dropping below it.

Below them, the sizing review that settled the band width, and the two placements for the project location that lost to the right-hand rail.

HOW TO SAY IT PRECISELY
The band is twelve columns summing to 1,482 px that divide into three exact thirds at G:J, K:N and O:R. A panel spans one third, anchored column to column. Three across, every row.

Aligned means more than equal panels: the plot rectangles inside them share a left inset, a top and a bottom, so three neighbouring y axes form one vertical line and three baselines form one horizontal line. That is the thing you look at and call aligned.

The tables start under the last chart row, on the same twelve columns, so their column edges land on the panel edges above them.

WHAT IT COST TO GET THERE
The gap between plots, measured off the rendered page rather than the file, before and after each move. Four of the things on the spec's failure list were in the workbook at some point in the last four rounds, and every one of them left the numbers in the XML looking correct.
